messages.author: cea45db0d664fec9
messages.subject: Single night sleep analysis
parts:
Hi all,

We are interested in analyzing single nights of sleep data to compare with in-lab PSG. Thus far, we have worked off Vincent's 2018 paper which recommends expanding the dataset by 90 min of simulated data to assist with SPT detection.

Does anyone recommend other strategies beyond this for single night analyses?

If this is the recommended approach, how can the simulated data be identified from the output?

Thanks for your help!
-Sarah

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Single night sleep analysis
parts:
Hi Sarah,

In case any of the following is helpful:
  • I used custom code: https://github.com/wadpac/psg-ncl-acc-spt-detection-eval tailored to the specific data sets I used for that study. The README file describes the key steps.
  • If your aim is to only evaluate sleep/wake classification without identification of the SPT window then the addition of simulated data is probably not necessary, because this classification is done per epoch and does not rely on algorithms to identify the largest episode of inactivity in a day. 
  • If you want to include SPT window detection then the addition of artificial data may be done at two levels:
    • raw: Export data to csv file and append synthetic data to start and end, next process the csv files with GGIR. 
    • epoch evel data: Go to GGIR part 1 output and append synthetic data to start and end.

Best,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.author: e246b463ba88b8d6
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Single night sleep analysis
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thank you very much for your previous reply. It's very inspiring. I am from Sarah's team and we do want to include SPT window detection. So we tried the "RAW" level that you mentioned in your reply on two of our files but we met several problems during the process:
1. we were not able to get the part 5 output
2. we only got one file processed to part 4 output
3. the numbers of part 4 output seemed to be different from what we expected (for example: sleeponset:25.333; wakeup: 26.332; SptDuration: 0.99, we thought that it would be a longer sleep duration)
We wondered if we were doing anything wrong in adding the artificial physical activity data or our codes were wrong. It would be great if you could give us some suggestions regarding it. The files were too large to upload here, so I had to create a google folder for the files (very sorry for the inconvenience): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/15gEtexoOyu6bhs78AwmGhBtg7uFZIDHc?usp=share_link

Our original csv files are (2 files): 7514033122_aligned_data_original and 7514072622_aligned_data_original
Our csv files with added 90-min PA to start and end are (2 files): 7514033122_aligned_data and 7514072622_aligned_data
We used the following codes to process the csv files with added 90-min PA to start and end without sleep log:

library(GGIR)
datadir="V:/.../add_90min_before_after_fake_v2"
outputdir="V:/.../output"

g.shell.GGIR(
  mode=c(1:5),
  datadir=datadir,
  outputdir=outputdir,
  studyname="Attempt1",
  idloc=2,
  f0=1,
  f1=2,
  print.filename=FALSE,
  storefolderstructure = FALSE,
  do.parallel=TRUE,
  overwrite=TRUE,
 
#part 1#
        windowsizes = c(5,600,600), #windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
        do.anglez=TRUE,
        chunksize = c(1),
        printsummary=TRUE,
 
#part 2#
        strategy = 1 , # strategy = 2
        hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0, #newly added by XZ to fit the one-day pa
        includedaycrit = 0.1, M5L5res = 10, #includedaycrit = 16
        winhr = 5,
        qwindow=c(0,24),
        qwindow_dateformat = "%d/%m/%Y",
        qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
        ilevels = c(0,36, 201, 707, 8000),
        mvpathreshold = c(201),
        boutcriter = 0.8,
          bout.metric = 6 ,
        epochvalues2csv=TRUE,
        mvpadur=c(1,5,10),
        iglevels = TRUE, #this function calculates intensity gradient

#part3#
        timethreshold= c(5),
        acc.metric="ENMO",
        anglethreshold=5,
        ignorenonwear = TRUE,

#part4#
       
        def.noc.sleep=1,
        includenightcrit = 1, #changed from 4 to 1
        outliers.only = TRUE,
        relyonguider = FALSE,
        criterror = 4,
        do.visual = FALSE,
        #nnights = 30,
       
#part 5#
        threshold.lig = c(35.6),
        threshold.mod = c(201.4),
        threshold.vig = c(707.0),
          #Hildebrand 2014 and 2016 intensity thresholds#
        excludefirstlast = FALSE,
        boutcriter = 0.8,
        boutcriter.in = 0.9,
        boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
        boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
        boutdur.in = c(10),
        boutdur.lig = c(1),
        boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
        timewindow = c("WW"),
        save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE, #newly added by XZ to save the time series classification (levels) as csv

do.report=c(2,4,5),
dofirstpage=TRUE,
visualreport=TRUE,
viewingwindow=1)

In addition, I also attached the output generated to the google folder as well. Hope it can provide some information. Sincerely thanks again for your time and help. 

Julia
